source_findings.finding: TemporalKG keeps an append-oriented fact_assertions history with valid_from/valid_to, superseded_by and invalidation_reason, supports point-in-time queries and diffs, and returns an existing id for a currently-valid exact (subject,predicate,object) duplicate.

TemporalKG.add_fact defaults invalidate_previous=true: a new object for the same subject/predicate can close currently-valid older assertions and commit the change directly to its SQLite database; source defaults source='auto'.

SkillStore keeps procedural steps, anti-patterns, learned_from lineage, versions and usage metrics, but record_use accepts a caller-supplied success boolean and automatically promotes a skill to active/mastered from usage count and success rate.

Episodic linking creates entity -> event -> knowledge graph structure around saves, but its documented failure mode is best-effort: graph errors are swallowed so the underlying knowledge save can proceed without the episodic projection.

GraphStore uses UUID ids and mutable reinforcement counters/weights; repeated node/edge observations increase mention/reinforcement state and cross-type name disagreements may reuse an existing node instead of forking a duplicate.
The quality gate uses an LLM-based specificity/actionability/verifiability score, but skip/error decisions are explicitly fail-open and allow the underlying save to proceed.

Vector storage is split between a Chroma adapter and a SQLite binary adapter; embedding provider/model/dimension/space/project identity is carried with vector records, while current SQLiteBinaryVectorStore writes remain routed through legacy Store code.
FactIndex is explicitly a structured/semantic retrieval prefilter over graph-derived data rather than an authority layer; it can embed graph triples into a derived semantic index.

The v13.0.1 release records a fixed write-path scaling defect: a ConceptExtractor was recreated on every save, causing one full graph_nodes read per save; upstream reports 1000 full reads per 1000 saves before and 1 after the fix.
The same release records BEAM-1M R@5=0.448 over 625 probes/74,630 messages and an unfixed search scaling issue where p50 grew to 411 ms because _binary_search is linear in active store size.

On exact upstream commit 6279a90370d32b8af5311816919fb2a6f5f6948d, GitHub Actions shows at least the push-triggered docker workflow completed with failure. No whole-upstream PASS is credited from workflow definitions or other runs.

donor_primitives.f2_shape: Keep valid_from/valid_to/superseded_by/invalidation_reason-style lineage, but derive changes only from admitted canonical evidence/events; never let a generated or auto-extracted assertion make itself current.

Store procedure version, learned_from provenance, anti-patterns and usage evidence as method memory; promotion/mastery requires verified outcome evidence or admitted evaluation, never an unverified caller boolean.

Use as a rebuildable graph/read projection derived from stable UnifiedDB causal/event identities. Projection failure may be nonblocking only when completeness is observable and deterministic rebuild is possible.
Preserve embedding provider/model/dimension/space and project/generation scope on derived index records so mixed embeddings cannot silently compare as one space.

donor_primitives.mechanism: structured fact prefilter plus semantic retrieval
donor_primitives.f2_shape: Use graph/semantic indexes only to rank candidate evidence references. Retrieval score, edge weight and reinforcement count never promote a fact.
May annotate candidate utility/quality. It cannot fail-open into canonical fact admission and cannot substitute typed provenance/evidence validation.

hypothesis: F2 can gain useful temporal, episodic and procedural memory behavior by distilling total-agent-memory's data-model ideas into typed UnifiedDB-backed canonical evidence plus disposable/rebuildable retrieval projections, without adopting its independent memory stores or its self-mutating truth/mastery semantics.
counterhypotheses: Existing F2 UnifiedDB plus Emergent Retrieval may already contain enough typed dimensions to implement these behaviors directly, making even a donor-shaped compatibility layer unnecessary.
The donor's benchmark gains may depend on graph extraction, embedding and benchmark-specific heuristics that do not transfer under F2's stricter causal/provenance constraints.
Temporal supersession and procedural promotion may add harmful false certainty if evidence authority is not explicitly separated from candidate memory representation.
At F2 scale, linear vector search and graph/retrieval maintenance cost may erase retrieval gains unless the derived index is replaced by a bounded scalable implementation.

cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.proposal: Use a synthetic, nonsecret, deterministic memory fixture containing fact supersessions, contradictions, repeated but false statements, verified/unverified procedure outcomes, project/generation boundaries and deletable derived indexes. First reproduce the narrow donor temporal/procedural behavior in an isolated temporary store; then compare against an F2-native UnifiedDB-derived projection on the identical fixture.
required_measurements: point-in-time fact precision and supersession correctness
false promotion rate from repeated but unverified observations
procedure mastery precision when outcomes are VERIFIED versus UNKNOWN
p50/p95/p99 query latency and CPU/RSS/I/O at increasing store sizes
cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.acceptance_signal: A distilled F2 projection improves retrieval or temporal/procedural usability while canonical UnifiedDB truth remains byte/identity stable under generated candidates, repeated false observations, projection deletion and provider failure.
cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.falsifier: No measurable retrieval/temporal benefit, any canonical-state mutation caused by derived memory, unresolved provenance leakage, unverified success causing mastery, non-rebuildable projection state, or unacceptable scaling overhead.
